title: US and South Korea to Conduct Military Drills Amid North Korean Threats
description:
South Korea and the United States announced major joint military drills scheduled from August 17 to 27, 2026, to counter evolving threats from North Korea. The exercises, part of the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS), will focus on countering drone attacks, GPS disruption, and cyber operations. Colonel Ryan Donald emphasized the need to adapt to North Korea's enhanced capabilities, which include lessons learned from their involvement in Ukraine. The drills will involve 18,000 South Korean troops and are aimed at bolstering emergency preparedness. North Korea has recently escalated its military posture, including missile launches and constitutional revisions that emphasize its nuclear capabilities. Despite claims of defensive intent, North Korea denounces these drills as provocations that exacerbate tensions. The situation remains critical as diplomatic relations between the two Koreas are at a low point.

Key Points:
• Joint military drills by US and South Korea scheduled from August 17 to 27, 2026.
• Focus on countering drone threats, GPS disruption, and cyberattacks from North Korea.
• North Korea's military posture has escalated, including recent missile tests.
